rows.conclusion: GL_n(Z) admissible iff n>=5; PGL_n(Z) admissible iff n=2 or n>=5.
route: I: final theorem and Sections 1–4, including both n=2 cases and all n>=5 words.
rows.qualification: PSL_3(2) and PSL_4(2) nonadmissibility are explicitly retained external inputs. No rank-three polytope conclusion over Z is asserted by this theorem.

rows.conclusion: GL_n(q) admissible iff [q=2 and (n=2 or n>=5)] or [q=3 and n>=5].
route: L: Theorem labelled gl, Section 2.
I supplies L's previously retained integral existence premise for reduction modulo 3.
U supplies the complete symmetric-square obstruction for GL_4(3).
rows.qualification: All q>=4 excluded by determinants; all n=3,4 excluded; GL_2(3) excluded directly. Source Table 1 is exactly these six cases.

rows.conclusion: GL_n(q) is a rank-three regular-polytope group iff q in {2,3} and n>=5.
route: L gives the complete admissibility exclusion list.
For q=3, GL_n(3)=H_n(3); H Theorem 1 gives generation and the actual intersection property.
For q=2, GL_n(2)=PSL_n(2) is simple for n>=5; retained simple admissibility and Conder–Oliveros give a marking.
GL_2(2)=S3 has no distinct commuting involutions and hence no rank-three C-marking.
Q Section 3 writes this complete assembly; its distinct review and root adoption are acquired.
rows.qualification: This is not a consequence of reducing integral generators alone. The replacement does not claim the precise source GL_6(3) marking or its pair orders 24 and 12.

rows.hypotheses: Finite field q; intended n>=2; d=gcd(n,q−1).
rows.conclusion: PGL_n(q) admissible iff n=2, or n>=4 and d=2, or n>=5 and d=1.
route: L: Theorem labelled pgl, Section 5, acquiring Sections 2–4 and U.
I replaces the old integral input in the q=3,n=6 reuse branch.
rows.qualification: For n=2 all q are positive, including q=2 by repeated marks. For n>=3, d>2 is excluded by the cyclic determinant quotient; n=3 is always negative; n=4,d=1 is negative. Source Table 2 is exactly these six cases.

rows.hypotheses: Finite field q; intended n>=2; d=gcd(n,q−1).
rows.conclusion: PGL_n(q) is a rank-three regular-polytope group iff n=2 and q!=2, or n>=4 and d=2, or n>=5 and d=1.
route: L: Section 5, paragraph following its two classification tables.
Q Section 3 repeats the exact parameter route and explicitly supplies the S3 exclusion.
rows.qualification: PGL_2(3)=S4 is not almost simple and is treated separately. For the other positive cases the simple-socle centralizer argument rules out cyclic normal subgroups. No blanket almost-simple assertion is retained.

rows.hypotheses: Odd prime power q; intended n>=2; H_n(q)={g:det(g)=±1}.
route: H: Theorem 1, all constructions in Sections 1–4.
Z: Theorem labelled small gives the complete n=2,3,4 exclusions using U.
rows.qualification: The characteristic-two sentence before the source theorem is background attributed to previous work, not an additional principal classification in this thesis.

rows.conclusion: H_n(q) is a rank-three regular-polytope group iff n>=5; for every n>=5 a type [4p,n] or [4p,2n] occurs.
route: H: Theorem 1 and Section 5, complete monomial-intersection calculation and exact product orders.
Z: n=2,3,4 nonadmissibility also excludes polytopes.
rows.qualification: The disjunction of types means at least one displayed construction of one of those types; it is not a classification of all possible types, nor a claim both types occur for every parameter.

rows.hypotheses: Odd q=p^m; even n>=6; Z1=Z(H_n(q)); d=gcd(n,q−1), e=(q−1)/d.
rows.conclusion: The full-centre quotient has a rank-three regular polytope of type [4p,n]. The printed universal isomorphism to PSL_n(q) semidirect C2 requires correction.
route: Z: Theorem labelled centres: H/Z1=PSL_n(q) for e even; H/Z1 embeds as PSL_n(q) semidirect C2 for e odd.

rows.qualification: Source p69 falsely states Z1=Z2 for every even n. At n=6,q=5, 2I has determinant −1, |Z1|=4 and |Z2|=2. This is a correction to a numbered corollary, not just a harmless intermediate typo.

rows.conclusion: H_n(q)/Z1 is PSL_n(q), with a rank-three regular polytope of type [4p,n].
route: Z: Theorem centres; odd n makes e even.
H: Theorem 2 with S=Z1.

rows.conclusion: H_n(q)/Z2 is PSL_n(q) × C2, with a rank-three regular polytope of type [4p,n] or [4p,2n].
route: Z: Theorem centres; the central factor is represented by −I.
